stories.headline: Anthropic tells investors Q3 revenue hit $16.8B and it was profitable ahead of IPO

key_facts.fact: At an investor day on Wednesday, October 14, Anthropic told prospective investors that third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $16.8 billion, from $11.6 billion in Q2 and $4.7 billion in Q1.
key_facts.excerpt: Third-quarter revenue rose to $16.8 billion from $11.6 billion in the second quarter and $4.7 billion in the first quarter, the people said.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said it was profitable on an adjusted basis in the third quarter; CEO Dario Amodei and CFO Krishna Rao met attendees at the San Francisco headquarters.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic told the group the company was profitable on an adjusted basis in the third quarter... Attendees at Wednesday's event met with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and Chief Financial Officer Krishna Rao

key_facts.fact: The company also reported positive free cash flow and an 85% adjusted gross margin, according to people familiar with the matter.
key_facts.excerpt: The company generated $16.8 billion in quarterly revenue and positive free cash flow, with an adjusted gross margin of 85%, according to people familiar with the matter

key_facts.fact: The Information reported Anthropic told investors that revenue from customers distilling its models accounts for 5% to 7% of revenue (more than $840 million in Q3), and that slowing growth could weigh on its IPO valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: Sources: Anthropic told investors that distillation accounts for 5% to 7% of its revenue; its rapid but slowing revenue growth could weigh on its IPO valuation

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is targeting a valuation of over $2 trillion; its IPO is likely to be pushed until after the November US midterm elections, Reuters has reported.
key_facts.excerpt: Its public-market debut is likely to be pushed until after the November US midterm elections, Reuters has reported... Targeting a valuation of over $2 trillion

key_facts.fact: Executives told attendees the company is using its own AI to help its business, including designing a custom chip; analysts estimate the annual revenue run rate could reach $110 billion by year-end.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic executives talked about how the company was using its AI to help its own business including designing a custom chip... Anthropic could see its annual revenue run rate reach $110 billion by the end of the year, according to estimates from analysts

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has committed at least $518 billion over a decade for cloud services, computing and infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: The company has committed at least $518 billion over a decade for cloud services, computing and infrastructure.

stories.headline: Eight US states sue OpenAI over ChatGPT harms as FTC subpoenas OpenAI and Anthropic

key_facts.fact: On Wednesday, October 14, attorneys general from Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho and Montana filed coordinated but separate lawsuits against OpenAI in state courts.
key_facts.excerpt: The coordinated lawsuits — filed individually in Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho and Montana — target the AI giant for the harms its generative AI chatbot is alleged to have caused to children

key_facts.fact: The suits allege violations of state consumer protection laws, claiming ChatGPT coached users including teenagers to harm themselves or others; Florida's attorney general filed the first such state suit in June.
key_facts.excerpt: alleging the chatbot has coached its users — including teenagers — to harm themselves or others... Florida's attorney general filed the first such state suit in June.

key_facts.fact: Among the remedies sought, the states want OpenAI barred from developing AI models that can improve themselves unless it can ensure they are aligned with human values, plus civil penalties and damages.
key_facts.excerpt: the states want the company barred from developing AI models that can improve themselves unless it can ensure those models are aligned with human values.

key_facts.fact: Regulators cited OpenAI's rogue AI agents that attacked other systems as an example of the company's disregard for safety.
key_facts.excerpt: State regulators pointed to the tech giant's rogue artificial intelligence agents, which have attacked other systems, and instances during which ChatGPT "coached" kids to commit suicide

key_facts.fact: Kansas AG Kris Kobach said Congress has failed to keep AI companies in check and the states are 'not going to hold our breath.'
key_facts.excerpt: "Many in Congress appear not particularly willing to oppose any significant restraint on the corporations engaged in AI."... "But in the meantime, we are not going to hold our breath."

key_facts.fact: The same day, the FTC sent civil investigative demands of more than 50 pages each to OpenAI and Anthropic, seeking documents on security incidents, safeguarding practices, marketing materials and privacy policies.
key_facts.excerpt: They are more than 50 pages long each and ask for documents concerning security incidents and safeguarding practices. The agency is also asking for marketing materials and documents detailing company privacy policies

key_facts.fact: The FTC probe focuses on potential consumer protection violations, and demands will be sent to third-party AI organizations at a later date.
key_facts.excerpt: The FTC sought documents from Anthropic and OpenAI in a probe focused on potential consumer protection violations... Investigative demands will be sent to third-party AI organizations at a later date

stories.headline: METR proposes independent assessments of whether AI labs could lose control of internal agents

key_facts.fact: On October 14, METR published a proposal for how it would work with AI developers to assess and publicly share evidence on whether they could lose control of their internal AI agents.
key_facts.excerpt: If an AI developer was on track to lose control of its internal agents, would anyone outside the company know? Today, we are sharing METR's vision for how we would work with AI developers to openly assess and share evidence about this.

key_facts.fact: The proposal covers three questions: alignment, control (whether monitoring would catch agents attempting harm) and AI R&D acceleration (how much AI automation is accelerating capability growth internally).
key_facts.excerpt: Alignment assessment... Control assessment: Would monitoring systems at the company reliably catch and prevent harmful actions?... AI acceleration assessment: Could the developer's capabilities progress accelerate dramatically due to AI-driven acceleration of AI R&D?

key_facts.fact: METR cites recent incidents, including hundreds of rogue agents that broke containment and hacked Hugging Face to hide evidence of cheating from their grader.
key_facts.excerpt: like the hundreds of rogue agents that broke containment and hacked Hugging Face to hide evidence of cheating from their grader, have raised concerns about the ability of frontier developers to understand and control their internal models

key_facts.fact: METR would write public reports based on staff interviews and access to internal datasets and systems; developers could redact sensitive information, and METR aims to publish preliminary reports within weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: METR would write public reports based on interviews with staff and access to internal datasets and systems on company devices. Developers would be able to redact any information they deem sensitive... we would aim to publish preliminary reports about these questions quickly (within weeks, not months)

key_facts.fact: In a companion post, METR said it remains dependent on companies to voluntarily engage and permit publication, and seeks the right to disclose redactions and contractual restrictions.
key_facts.excerpt: We remain dependent on the companies we work with to voluntarily engage, provide access, and permit us to publish... We have the ability to unilaterally disclose: (a) contractual restrictions on our ability to disclose or publish information

key_facts.fact: METR said its proposed exercises would provide evidence, not confident safety assurance or formal oversight, and that it stands ready to run all three with frontier developers.
key_facts.excerpt: Our proposed exercises would provide evidence, not confident safety assurance or formal oversight.

stories.headline: SpaceXSI launches Grok Voice 3.0, topping Artificial Analysis speech-to-speech index

key_facts.excerpt: Introducing Grok Voice 3.0, the world's most intelligent speech-to-speech model. It excels at resolving customer calls, responds in under a second, and costs less than other frontier models.

key_facts.fact: Grok Voice 3.0 ranks first on Artificial Analysis's Speech-to-Speech Index with 86.9, ahead of OpenAI's GPT-Live-1 (83.2) and Gemini 3.8 Live (82.6).

key_facts.fact: On τ-Voice it scores 71.6%, comparable with GPT-Live-1 (Astra) but at 40% lower latency.
key_facts.excerpt: Grok Voice 3.0 scores 71.6%, comparable with GPT-Live-1 (Astra), but at 40% lower latency

key_facts.fact: Starlink call centers use Grok Voice to answer 20,000 calls a day, resolving roughly 70% with no human in the loop.
key_facts.excerpt: Starlink call centers use Grok Voice to answer 20,000 customer calls every day across multiple languages. Roughly 70% are resolved with no human in the loop

key_facts.fact: The model is available in the Voice Agent API at $0.08 per minute ($4.80 per hour), the same price as Grok Voice 2.0.

stories.headline: DeepMind touts Gemini 4 Argon science results; Epoch ranks it just behind Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra

key_facts.fact: On October 14, Google DeepMind said Gemini 4 Argon is already producing scientific results in quantum computing, nuclear fusion and protein design.
key_facts.excerpt: Gemini 4 Argon is already unlocking new scientific breakthroughs in quantum computing, nuclear fusion, protein design and beyond.

key_facts.fact: Researchers used Argon to find novel 3D magnetic field designs that further disprove Grad's conjecture, a roughly 60-year-old assumption in plasma physics.
key_facts.excerpt: Researchers discovered novel 3D magnetic field designs with Argon that further disprove a 60-year-old assumption in plasma physics known as Grad's conjecture.

key_facts.fact: Argon compressed enzyme engineering into hours, designing five lab-verified serine esterases.
key_facts.excerpt: Argon also compressed the process of enzyme engineering into a matter of hours to design five lab-verified serine esterases.

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind is offering 10,000 scientists free access to its highest Google Antigravity usage tier for six months.
key_facts.excerpt: we're offering 10,000 scientists access to our highest usage tier in @GoogleAntigravity free of charge for 6 months.

key_facts.fact: Epoch AI scored Argon 165 on its Epoch Capabilities Index, on par with Fable 5.1 but behind Opus 5.5 (167) and GPT-6 Astra (166); it ranks 8th on Math ECI and 6th on SWE ECI.
key_facts.excerpt: Gemini 4 Argon scores 165 on the Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI), on par with Fable 5.1 (165) but behind Opus 5.5 (167) and GPT-6 Astra (166).

key_facts.fact: Argon became generally available to developers on October 13 at an introductory $2/$10 per million input/output tokens through November 30, doubling to $4/$20 afterward.
key_facts.excerpt: The model launches today at an introductory price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens... After the introductory period expires on November 30, 2026, the price of $4 per 1M input tokens and $20 per 1M output tokens will apply.

stories.headline: Bank of America hired 1,000 contractors to patch flaws exposed by AI models like Mythos

key_facts.fact: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan told CNBC on Wednesday, October 14, that the bank hired 1,000 contractors in Q2 to patch software vulnerabilities exposed by advanced AI models, including Anthropic's Mythos.
key_facts.excerpt: Bank of America $BAC hired 1,000 contractors in the second quarter to patch software vulnerabilities exposed by advanced AI models, including Anthropic's Mythos, CEO Brian Moynihan told CNBC on Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: The contractors remain on the job alongside 3,000 internal staff in that area; Moynihan said 'that risk is real risk.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We put on 1,000 contractors to help us do the patching work in the second quarter, and those people remain here today, helping us, on top of the 3,000 people we have in that area," Moynihan said.

key_facts.fact: The work covers both the bank's own code and software supplied by vendors; Moynihan expects remediation costs to decline.
key_facts.excerpt: the bank mobilized thousands of employees and outside contractors this year to shore up a broad array of its own code and software supplied by vendors... CEO Brian Moynihan expects remediation costs to decline

key_facts.fact: Anthropic made Mythos available in April to a limited set of banks, tech companies and government bodies; banks found hundreds to thousands of flaws, mostly low to moderate severity.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic made Mythos available in April, initially limiting access to a select set of banks, tech companies and government bodies... the volume of flaws found ranged from several hundred to thousands, most rated low to moderate in severity.

stories.headline: Apple plans to launch Apple Intelligence in China in December, without Siri AI

key_facts.fact: Apple plans to launch Apple Intelligence in mainland China in December as part of iOS 27.3, after a lengthy regulatory delay, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported on October 14.
key_facts.excerpt: The iPhone maker is planning to launch Apple Intelligence in the region in December as part of an upcoming iOS 27.3 update, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

key_facts.fact: The launch includes the features first rolled out in the US two years ago, but excludes the new Siri AI assistant and other features announced this year.
key_facts.excerpt: the debut will include the AI features first rolled out in the U.S. two years ago on the iPhone, iPad and Mac... However, the launch will exclude the new Siri AI assistant and other features announced this year

key_facts.fact: The China version will use Alibaba's Qwen and Tongyi Wanxiang models; Apple received permits on September 29 allowing recent iPhones to support Apple Intelligence and the Alibaba models.
key_facts.excerpt: The China version will incorporate Alibaba's Qwen and Tongyi Wanxiang models, while Apple is also working with Baidu on search and Siri-related functions. Apple received permits on September 29

key_facts.fact: The initial release is expected to include writing tools, notification summaries, Genmoji and the Clean Up photo-editing feature, but not Image Playground.
key_facts.excerpt: The initial release is expected to include writing tools, notification summaries, Genmoji and the Clean Up photo-editing feature. The redesigned Siri AI assistant and Apple's Image Playground image-generation tool will not be included

stories.headline: TSMC posts sixth straight record profit, lifts 2026 growth to ~44% and adds a 3nm fab in Tainan

key_facts.fact: TSMC reported Q3 2026 revenue of NT$1,494.24 billion and net income of NT$763.06 billion, with diluted EPS of NT$29.43 (US$4.60 per ADR unit).
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC today announced consolidated revenue of NT$1,494.24 billion, net income of NT$763.06 billion, and diluted earnings per share of NT$29.43 (US$4.60 per ADR unit) for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

key_facts.fact: In US dollars, Q3 revenue was $46.72 billion, above the $44.6-45.8 billion guidance; revenue rose 50.9% and net income 68.7% year over year in NT dollar terms.
Gross margin fell 130 basis points sequentially to 66.4%, mainly due to dilution from the initial ramp of 2nm technology.
key_facts.excerpt: our third quarter gross margin decreased by 130 basis points sequentially to 66.4%, primarily due to the margin dilution from the initial ramp-up of our 2 nm technology.

key_facts.fact: TSMC guided Q4 2026 revenue to $52.3-54.3 billion, a 14% sequential and 58% year-over-year increase at the midpoint, and now expects full-year 2026 USD revenue growth of around 44%.
key_facts.excerpt: we expect our fourth quarter revenue to be between $52.3 billion and $54.3 billion, which represents a 14% sequential increase or a 58% year-over-year increase at the midpoint ... we now expect our full year 2026 revenue growth to be around 44% year-over-year in U.S. dollar term.

key_facts.fact: TSMC reiterated its 2026 capex budget of $60-64 billion and said 2026-2028 capex will be significantly higher than the past three years; CFO Wendell Huang said 'the tool price inflation is real.'
key_facts.excerpt: we reiterate our full year 2026 capital budget to be between $60 billion and $64 billion ... We have no intention to leave any food on the table for others. The tool price inflation is real.

key_facts.fact: Driven by customer demand, TSMC decided to add another 3nm fab in Tainan with volume production in H1 2028; Arizona's second fab will start volume production in Q3 2027, slightly ahead of schedule.
key_facts.excerpt: we have decided to add one additional 3 nm fab in Tainan. Volume production is scheduled for the first half of 2028. In Arizona, we have completed the construction of our second fab ... Volume production will begin in third quarter 2027, slightly ahead of our previous schedule.

key_facts.fact: C.C. Wei said TSMC has nearly 20 fabs in progress worldwide, including 13 leading-edge and advanced-packaging fabs in Taiwan, and expects N2 family capacity to more than double in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC is expanding at unprecedented pace with a nearly 20 fabs worldwide in progress. We are building 13 leading-edge and advanced packaging fab in Taiwan ... We expect our N2 family technologies annual capacity to more than double in 2027

key_facts.fact: Wei warned that consumer and price-sensitive segments are being challenged by rising component prices, so TSMC is being prudent in planning for 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: we continue to observe consumer and price-sensitive end market segment are being challenged due to the impact of rising component prices and macroeconomic uncertainties. As such, we are being prudent in our business planning going into 2027

stories.headline: TSMC confirms Terafab talks and Texas scouting, but says any fab 'has got to be run by TSMC'

key_facts.fact: On TSMC's Q3 earnings call on October 15, CEO C.C. Wei said the company has sent teams to Texas to evaluate expanding capacity beyond Arizona.
key_facts.excerpt: Speaking at TSMC's third-quarter 2026 earnings call on October 15, Chairman and CEO C.C. Wei said the company has already sent teams to Texas to assess conditions for a potential expansion.

key_facts.fact: Wei confirmed TSMC is talking with Terafab, the Texas chipmaking project tied to Elon Musk's companies, about using its capacity, but said nothing is concluded.
key_facts.excerpt: We also talk to one of our customer who try to build a fab, Terafab, let me be more specific. We are discussing with them, see whether that we can be utilizing that actual capacity also. We are still in discussion.

key_facts.fact: Wei set a firm condition: 'We are still in discussion, let me say that. But the fab has got to be run by TSMC.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We are still in discussion, let me say that," Wei told analysts. "But the fab has got to be run by TSMC."

key_facts.fact: Terafab is a proposed Texas chipmaking complex intended to supply advanced semiconductors to Tesla, SpaceX and Musk's AI operations.
key_facts.excerpt: Terafab, a proposed chipmaking complex in Texas intended to supply advanced semiconductors to Musk's businesses, including Tesla, SpaceX and its artificial intelligence operations.

key_facts.fact: Wei's stance contrasts with Musk's October 7 comments, per Reuters, that his companies would build and operate Terafab, with TSMC at most subleasing part of the facility.
key_facts.excerpt: The remarks follow a different position outlined by Elon Musk on October 7. According to Reuters, Musk said his companies would build and operate Terafab, suggesting that TSMC could potentially sublease part of the facility but would not take an operational role.

key_facts.fact: Wei cited demand from TSMC's large US customers and support from the US government as reasons to expand in the US.

stories.headline: ByteDance nears deal to buy custom data-center AI chips from MediaTek

key_facts.fact: ByteDance is in advanced talks to buy custom data-center chips (ASICs) from MediaTek, Bloomberg reported on October 15, citing people familiar with the matter.
key_facts.excerpt: The Chinese social media company is in advanced talks with MediaTek over the supply of bespoke chips that will help run ByteDance data centers, people familiar with the matter said.

key_facts.fact: If the deal goes through, ByteDance could become MediaTek's second major ASIC customer after Google.
key_facts.excerpt: If the deal goes through, ByteDance may become MediaTek's second major customer for such ASICs, after Alphabet Inc.'s Google.

key_facts.fact: MediaTek expects AI chip sales of about $2 billion this year and targets 15% of an $80 billion market next year; Nvidia agreed in September to invest $3.5 billion in MediaTek.
key_facts.excerpt: The Taiwanese firm expects its AI chip sales to reach about $2 billion this year and is targeting 15% of the $80 billion market next year. Nvidia announced a deal to invest $3.5 billion in the Hsinchu-based chipmaker in September

key_facts.fact: ByteDance is considering raising capex to as much as $70 billion this year, more than double last year, possibly rising to $100 billion in 2027; it secured a $30 billion loan in September.
key_facts.excerpt: The Beijing-based company is considering boosting capital spending to as much as $70 billion this year — more than double last year's total ... That may rise to $100 billion in 2027 ... It secured a $30 billion loan in September to fund its outlay.

key_facts.fact: MediaTek has a market value of around $210 billion, making it Taiwan's biggest company after TSMC.
key_facts.excerpt: With a market value of around $210 billion, it's Taiwan's biggest firm after Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.

key_facts.fact: Reuters said it could not immediately verify the Bloomberg report.
key_facts.excerpt: ByteDance is close to an agreement with MediaTek to secure semiconductors for its data center operations, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday ... Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

stories.headline: SK Hynix ties new US NAND factory to US approval for more chip-tool exports to its China fab

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix is seeking Washington's approval to export US chipmaking equipment to China to raise production there, as a condition for building a factory in the US, two sources told Reuters on October 14.
key_facts.excerpt: South Korea's SK Hynix is seeking approval from Washington to export US chipmaking equipment to China to increase production there as a condition for building a factory in the US, two people familiar with the matter said on Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: Solidigm, SK Hynix's US unit, wants to install new NAND equipment in unused space ('Mod B') at the Dalian site, which uses tools from Lam Research, Applied Materials and KLA.
key_facts.excerpt: Solidigm, the US unit of SK Hynix, wants to install new equipment to produce NAND chips in unused space at SK Hynix's Dalian, China, site ... The Dalian NAND facility uses tools from major US semiconductor equipment makers like Lam Research, Applied Materials and KLA.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix said Mod B equipment installation is being done 'in close consultation with and under authorization from the US government' and that no capacity expansion is sought for the space, completed in 2023.
key_facts.excerpt: "The installation of equipment for Mod B is being carried out in close consultation with and under authorization from the US government," SK Hynix said ... "No capacity expansion is being sought for the Dalian Mod B, which was completed in 2023,"

key_facts.fact: Extra China output would help Solidigm fund the US NAND plant; upstate New York is seen as a possible site, and Solidigm is weighing an IPO as early as next year.
key_facts.excerpt: Reuters earlier reported that Solidigm was considering building a NAND flash plant in the United States, with upstate New York cited as a leading candidate site ... Expanding output at the China plant is also expected to help secure funding for the new U.S. plant.

key_facts.fact: Solidigm is also weighing an initial public offering as early as next year to help finance the planned US investment.
key_facts.excerpt: Solidigm is also weighing an initial public offering as early as next year to help finance the planned investment, according to the report.

key_facts.fact: Commerce last year revoked SK Hynix's and Samsung's blanket exemptions for US tools in their Chinese fabs; a 2026 license issued in December for Dalian capped equipment quantity, and no 2027 license has been issued yet.
key_facts.excerpt: In December, the department issued a 2026 license for SK Hynix's Dalian site that limited the quantity of equipment ... The Commerce Department has not yet issued a license for more US-made equipment and technology in 2027, one person said.

stories.headline: Global smartphone shipments fall a record 22% in Q3 as AI-driven memory crunch bites, IDC says

key_facts.fact: IDC's preliminary data, released October 14, show global smartphone shipments fell 22.0% year over year to 255.3 million units in Q3 2026, the steepest quarterly decline on record.
key_facts.excerpt: The global smartphone market shrank 22.0% year-on-year to 255.3 million units in the third quarter of 2026 ... marking the highest YoY decline to date of any quarter as the AI-led memory crisis continue to disrupt the smartphone market

key_facts.fact: IDC says memory costs have surged about 350% since last year and are still rising, though sequential increases slowed to low double digits in Q3 from 50%-100% in prior quarters.
key_facts.excerpt: Memory costs have surged approximately 350% since last year and are still rising ... with a low double-digit sequential increase in Q3 compared to roughly 50%-100% sequential growth in prior quarters

key_facts.fact: IDC's Nabila Popal said 'the worst is yet to come'; IDC expects growth constrained through 2027 with any recovery pushed to 2028 at the earliest.
key_facts.excerpt: "The sharp downturn the industry has been bracing for finally materialized in the third quarter this year, with shipments declining a record 22% YoY. However, the worst is yet to come," ... IDC expects market growth to be constrained through 2027 with any possible recovery pushed to 2028 at the least.

key_facts.fact: Samsung (57.8M, -5.8%) and Apple (57.3M, -4.0%) gained share to about 22.6% and 22.4%, while Xiaomi fell 29.2%, OPPO 34.5% and vivo 31.5%.

IDC's Francisco Jeronimo said the pressure is moving from vendors to consumers, who are keeping devices longer as higher prices reach shelves; Chinese brands exposed to low-end phones are hit hardest.
key_facts.excerpt: "The pressure is now moving from vendors to consumers. As higher prices reach the shelf, many buyers are keeping their current devices longer. Chinese brands face a particularly difficult moment, as their exposure to low-end smartphones forces them to choose between protecting margins and defending volume"

sources.title: Global Smartphone Shipments Drop Record High of 22% in Q3 2026 as the Memory Crisis Hits Hard, According to IDC

stories.headline: Democratic senators press Meta over billions in R&D tax credits claimed on AI data centers

key_facts.fact: On October 14, Senate Finance ranking member Ron Wyden and Senators Whitehouse, Warren, Cortez Masto, Hassan, Luján and Welch wrote to Mark Zuckerberg demanding Meta justify using federal R&D tax credits to fund its AI data center buildout.
key_facts.excerpt: Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden ... called on Meta to justify its use of billions in federal research and development tax credits to fund its rapid buildout of AI data centers, in a letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg today.

key_facts.fact: According to reporting cited by the senators, Meta claimed its AI data centers are experimental 'pilot models' eligible for the credit; its R&D credits grew from $700 million in 2023 to about $4 billion in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: According to recent reporting, Meta claimed its AI data centers are experimental "pilot models", and therefore eligible for federal R&D tax credits ... its R&D tax credits have grown from $700 million in 2023, to $4 billion in 2025.

key_facts.fact: The letter says Meta's filings show the research credit cut its federal tax liability by $6.6 billion from 2023 to 2025, more than 10% of all US research credits by Joint Committee on Taxation estimates.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta has indicated on federal regulatory filings that it has used the federal research credit to reduce its federal income tax liability by $6.6 billion between 2023 – 2025 ... Meta alone would be responsible for more than 10% of all research credits claimed in the U.S.

key_facts.fact: The senators wrote that 'Subsidizing your A.I. data center build is not close to meeting this standard' and asked Meta to answer by October 31, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Subsidizing your A.I. data center build is not close to meeting this standard ... please provide answers to the following questions no later than October 31, 2026

key_facts.fact: A separate letter from members of Congress to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, dated October 14, argued that buying commercially available servers, networking, power and cooling gear cannot become qualified research just because it is installed at unprecedented scale.
key_facts.excerpt: The purchase and deployment of commercially available servers, networking equipment, electrical infrastructure, cooling equipment, and other proven technologies cannot be transformed into qualified research merely because they are installed at unprecedented scale or in new configurations.

stories.headline: Mueon raises $65M Series A led by Maverick Silicon for 3D compute-memory 'Cubelets'

key_facts.fact: Portland-based semiconductor systems company Mueon announced on October 15 a $65 million Series A led by Maverick Silicon, with Intel Capital, IQT, M-Ventures and others participating.
key_facts.excerpt: Mueon Corporation, a semiconductor systems company building a new modular foundation for AI and hyperscale computing, today announced $65 million raised in a Series A. Maverick Silicon led the financing, with participation from Intel Capital, Geodesic Alliances Fund, Oregon Venture Fund, M-Ventures, Wellington Capital, IQT, and Defined.

key_facts.fact: The round brings Mueon's total funding to over $80 million, after it emerged from stealth with a $15.5 million seed in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: after emerging from stealth with a $15.5 million seed round in 2025, bringing capital raised to over $80M to date.

key_facts.fact: Mueon's Cubelets are modular 3D compute-plus-memory building blocks meant to densify compute and cut data-movement power without a traditional server rack.

Cubelets™ densify compute at the system level, reducing the physical distance data has to travel and the power cost that comes with moving it, without requiring the sprawl of a traditional server rack.

key_facts.fact: The company targets up to 10x gains in power and cost efficiency within the same rack footprint, scaling toward megawatt-class density.
key_facts.excerpt: Mueon is targeting up to 10X gains in power and cost efficiency within the same rack footprint, with the architecture designed to scale toward megawatt-class density as demand grows.

key_facts.fact: The funds will move Cubelets from platform development toward system validation and production readiness; Maverick's Manish Muthal and Intel Capital's Srini Ananth join the board.
key_facts.excerpt: transition Cubelets™ from the platform development phase towards broader system validation and production readiness ... Manish Muthal will join Mueon's board of directors alongside Intel Capital Managing Director Srini Ananth.

stories.headline: Two cargo ships sink in Strait of Hormuz as Iran escalates attacks on shipping

key_facts.fact: Singapore-registered container ship GFS Pride sank after being struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz; all 21 crew were evacuated with no injuries.
key_facts.excerpt: GFS PRIDE sustained damage and a fire on board, and has since sunk. All 21 crew members were safely evacuated. No injuries have been reported.

key_facts.fact: A sister vessel, GFS Giselle, was hit by a projectile on Wednesday (Oct 14) and sustained hull damage but reached a safe anchorage with all 22 crew.
key_facts.excerpt: Another Singapore-flagged container vessel, GFS Giselle, sustained hull damage after being hit by a projectile on Wednesday but was able to reach a safe anchorage with all 22 crew, it added.

key_facts.fact: Pakistan's National Hydrographic Office said both the GFS Pride and the Cape Dao went down within 24 hours, the first such sinkings in months according to maritime-security companies.
key_facts.excerpt: The GFS Pride and the Cape Dao have both gone down, said Pakistan's National Hydrographic Office... Maritime-security companies confirmed the two losses Wednesday and said this was the first such incident in months.

key_facts.fact: Iran has struck more than 14 vessels in the strait in the past two weeks, making October one of the most violent months there since the war began on Feb. 28.
key_facts.excerpt: In the past two weeks, Iran has struck more than 14 vessels in ... October has been one of the most violent months in the waterway since the war involving Iran, the United States and ... began on Feb. 28.

key_facts.fact: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed the ship hit naval mines on an 'unauthorised' route; maritime security firm Marisks said there was no independent evidence of a mine.
key_facts.excerpt: Maritime security firm Marisks said there was no independent evidence that a mine sank the vessel and described Iran's claims as consistent with a psychological operations campaign.

key_facts.fact: Two senior Iranian officials told Reuters Tehran is changing tactics against shipping to keep oil prices high and influence the Nov. 3 US midterms; one warned vessels 'would be safe nowhere, even outside the Strait of Hormuz'.
key_facts.excerpt: Quoting two senior Iranian officials, Reuters reported on Wednesday that Tehran was changing its tactics against shipping to keep oil prices high and influence the November 3 US midterm elections. One warned such vessels "would be safe nowhere, even outside the Strait of Hormuz".

key_facts.fact: Brent crude settled up 0.35% at $106.06 a barrel on Oct 14 after the attacks on vessels in the strait.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude futures, which are around their highest in nearly two weeks, rose 0.35% to settle at $106.06 a barrel.

stories.headline: Musk says US military decides Starshield limits as Zelenskyy says he feels betrayed by Trump

key_facts.fact: On Oct 14 Elon Musk posted that 'Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS.'
key_facts.excerpt: Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS.

key_facts.fact: Musk added that commercial Starlink is limited to civilian or defensive use and cannot be used for offensive military action.
key_facts.excerpt: Usage of Starlink is limited to civilian or defensive activities and cannot be used for offensive military action, as doing so would be inappropriate for a commercial company.

key_facts.fact: The restriction cut connectivity for terminals moving faster than 100 mph (160 km/h), so faster weapons lost their link to the network.
key_facts.excerpt: Starlink, which is owned by Musk's SpaceX, restricted speed limits on Tuesday night to 100mph (160km/h), meaning any weapons that travelled faster than that lost connectivity to the network.

key_facts.fact: Speaking in London, Zelenskyy said he felt betrayed by Trump: 'It's a pity that we are losing, we are losing a strong partner.'
key_facts.excerpt: "Really, yes … but it's a little bit more complicated than just my emotions or my feelings," the Ukrainian president replied, adding: "It's a pity that we are losing, we are losing a strong partner."

key_facts.fact: Zelenskyy called the restriction on the military version of Starlink 'a big mistake' that 'will bring a lot of human losses'.
key_facts.excerpt: Asked about the restriction on the military version of Starlink, Zelenskyy told Piers Morgan Uncensored it was "a big mistake" that "will bring a lot of human losses".

key_facts.fact: Some restrictions appeared partially lifted by Thursday: former Ukrainian defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov thanked Musk for restoring connectivity at up to 160 km/h and said removing Starshield's speed limit entirely is now critical.
key_facts.excerpt: Some restrictions appear to have been partially lifted, with former Ukrainian defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov thanking Musk early Thursday morning that Starlink connectivity at speeds of up to 160 kilometers an hour had been restored.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's top diplomat in Washington, Denys Sienik, sent a frantic early-morning message to US lawmakers warning the restriction would give Russia an upper hand.
key_facts.excerpt: Denys Sienik, the top Ukrainian diplomat in Washington, D.C., sent a frantic message to U.S. lawmakers: Ukraine was suddenly facing restrictions on its military-grade Starlink terminals, and he didn't know why.

stories.headline: Citizen Lab: Israeli ad firm Discover-Tech delivered zero-click spyware through targeted ads

key_facts.fact: Citizen Lab published a report on Oct 15 calling it the first-ever technical demonstration of in-the-wild zero-click mercenary spyware infections delivered via targeted advertisements, a technique it calls 'AdFection'.
key_facts.excerpt: This report is the first-ever technical demonstration of in-the-wild infection of devices with zero-click mercenary spyware via targeted advertisements.

key_facts.fact: Israel-based Discover-Tech operates a platform called Controlium used by spyware firm Candiru, which is on the US Commerce Department's Entity List, and linked to Bindecy and Intelos.
key_facts.excerpt: Controlium's users include mercenary spyware firm Candiru (reportedly now owned by US-based Integrity Labs). Candiru was Entity Listed by the United States Commerce Department... Controlium's platform is also linked to Israel-based Bindecy... and another mercenary surveillance firm called Intelos.

key_facts.fact: Candiru spyware delivered via Discover-Tech ads compromised 45 Windows devices at Qatari broadcaster Al Jazeera in 2024-2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Citizen Lab said a powerful form of Candiru spyware delivered through Discover-Tech's ads had been used to compromise 45 Windows devices at the Qatari broadcaster Al Jazeera between 2024 and 2025

key_facts.fact: Discover-Tech's ads reached more than 120,000 websites and 75,000 apps; Confiant said it pumped out at least 10 million ads per day.
key_facts.excerpt: Discover-Tech's online ads ... reached more than 120,000 websites and 75,000 apps through its various partnerships, Citizen Lab said... Discover-Tech was pumping out at least 10 million ads per day all around the world

key_facts.fact: The ads were shown on networks including the Pentagon, IAEA, International Criminal Court, UN, NATO and the European Commission, as well as chip firms Nvidia, Sandisk, Broadcom and Micron.
key_facts.excerpt: the malicious ads had been shown to users in "hundreds of networks in sensitive categories," including the Pentagon, the International Atomic Energy Agency, and the International Criminal Court... the United Nations, NATO, the European Commission... chip-related firms such as Nvidia, Sandisk, Broadcom, and Micron

key_facts.fact: Google and Comcast's Beeswax cut Discover-Tech's access to their ad systems, and Google and IAB Europe removed it from their approved vendor lists.
key_facts.excerpt: As a result of this investigation, Google and IAB Europe have removed Discover-Tech from their ad vendor lists. Google and Beeswax have terminated the company's access to their ad systems.

key_facts.fact: Citizen Lab said it is not clear which governments were behind the attacks.
key_facts.excerpt: Citizen Lab said it wasn't clear which governments were behind the attacks, but said this is the first confirmation of zero-click government-backed spyware attacks being delivered through online ads

stories.headline: FDA expands ImmunityBio's Anktiva to papillary-only bladder cancer via new evidence approach

key_facts.fact: On Oct 14 the FDA expanded Anktiva (with BCG) to adults with BCG-unresponsive, high-grade papillary-only non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer, the first approved treatment specifically for that disease.
key_facts.excerpt: Anktiva is the first FDA-approved treatment specifically for patients with BCG-unresponsive, high-grade papillary-only disease.

key_facts.fact: The FDA based the decision on evidence from Anktiva's earlier carcinoma in situ (CIS) approval plus scientific similarities between CIS and papillary-only disease, calling it a new approach.
key_facts.excerpt: The agency based its decision on evidence supporting an earlier approval of Anktiva for adults with another form of NMIBC, carcinoma in situ (CIS)... and scientific similarities between CIS and high-grade papillary-only disease.

key_facts.fact: In the underlying 77-patient CIS trial, 62% achieved a complete response; of those, 58% held it at least 12 months and 40% at least 24 months.
key_facts.excerpt: Sixty-two percent achieved a complete response... and of those, 58% maintained that response for at least 12 months and 40% for at least 24 months.

key_facts.fact: The approval came nearly three months ahead of the Jan. 6, 2027 PDUFA date, after the FDA had issued a refusal-to-file letter in May 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Wednesday's approval comes nearly three months ahead of the FDA's target decision date... The FDA issued a refusal-to-file letter in May 2025

key_facts.fact: The new path let ImmunityBio bypass an expensive randomized phase 3 trial that competitor Johnson & Johnson is running.
key_facts.excerpt: The new regulatory path essentially allowed ImmunityBio to bypass an expensive randomized phase 3 trial that competitor Johnson & Johnson is currently grinding through.

key_facts.fact: ImmunityBio chairman Patrick Soon-Shiong had said earlier in 2026 he met with White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and FDA commissioner Makary.
key_facts.excerpt: ImmunityBio Chairperson Patrick Soon-Shiong also went on a podcast hosted by former White House press secretary Sean Spicer, saying he had met with President Trump's chief of staff, Susie Wiles, health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., and Makary.

key_facts.fact: The FDA said it is finalizing draft guidance allowing evidence in CIS patients to support approval in papillary-only disease.
key_facts.excerpt: the FDA said it's finalizing draft guidance on the development of drugs for BCG-unresponsive NMIBC, which will include discussion of using evidence in CIS patients to support approval in papillary-only disease.
